alt: Three rows of questions. What is produced: arable, pastoral or mixed. Who is it for: subsistence or commercial. How is it farmed: intensive or monoculture. A note says one farm can belong to several categories at once.
caption: Answer all three questions to classify a farm fully.

after: ## Strategies to increase food production and crop yield
alt: Five columns feed into higher crop yield. Water: trickle irrigation, rainwater harvesting, automated watering. Nutrients: crop rotation with legumes, NPK and organic fertilisers, agroforestry. Pests, weeds and disease: mixed cropping, pesticides, biological control, GMOs. Protect the soil: livestock rotation, agroforestry, mulch. More land, time or control: mechanisation, greenhouses, hydroponics and aeroponics, urban farming.
caption: For each strategy, say what limiting factor it removes.

after: ## Strategies to increase food production and crop yield
alt: Three sketches. A greenhouse where temperature, water and carbon dioxide are controlled. Hydroponics, with plant roots in a nutrient solution instead of soil. Aeroponics, with roots hanging in air and sprayed with a nutrient mist. Benefits and limitations are listed below.
caption: Control the conditions and crops grow faster, but at a cost in money and energy.

alt: Six numbered steps: fertiliser leaches into a river or lake; nitrate and phosphate enrich the water; algae grow rapidly over the surface; light is blocked so plants below die; bacteria decompose the dead material and use up oxygen; fish and other animals die. Below, a lake sketch shows algae on the surface and dead fish.
caption: Write every link: nutrients, algae, no light, decomposers, no oxygen, death.

alt: Sketch graph of pest and predator numbers over time. After insecticide is sprayed both fall; the predators stay low while the pest breeds quickly and rises above its original level. Cards distinguish pest resurgence from pesticide resistance.
caption: Kill the predators along with the pest and the pest comes back stronger.

alt: Bar chart of maize yield on a 40 hectare farm: 2.4 tonnes per hectare before and 3.0 after intercropping with beans and drip irrigation, a 25% increase.
